purpose: Test whether the frozen 8 s window accumulates too much frequency nonstationarity, changing only window_sec.

frozen.reference: non-causal resample_poly(5,2) + zero-phase butter 0.5-1.25 Hz + Hilbert

canonical_baseline.source: reproduced independently by P1, P3 and this P2 harness (MAE = 1.041248 rad)

historical_p0_artifact.status: provenance only; not an active baseline
historical_p0_artifact.reason: P0 runner subtracted the adapter group delay twice (segment slice offset plus index offset), shifting the offline reference by 8 samples = 32 ms

fft_grid_confound.exploratory_note: all correlations are over n = 9 candidate windows and are descriptive, not inferential

q1_peak_at_f0_bin_aligned_windows.evidence: the best-MAE window carries the largest f0-to-bin mismatch, so the peak does not sit at bin-aligned windows

q3_window_curve_shape.note: monotone degradation from 1.0 s to 2.0 s, then a plateau near 1.03-1.05 rad with a local bump at 2.0 s; the optimum sits on the shortest-window boundary of the grid, not at an interior short-optimum-long-worsening minimum

q4_best_candidate_explained_by_grid.conclusion: the narrow f0-to-bin alignment mechanism is not supported, but the number of in-band FFT bins is a deterministic, rank-collinear function of the swept window length, so this design cannot attribute the short-window gain to temporal window length alone

fft_grid_confound.decision_rule: selection is allowed only if no FFT-grid diagnostic is rank-collinear with window length (|rho| >= 0.9) and no diagnostic shows a strong monotone relationship with MAE/q95/R (|rho| >= 0.5)
